question.problem: A fair twelve-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $1$ through $12$ is rolled $80$ times. What is the standard deviation of the number of times we get a number divisible by $5?$
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be the number of times we get a number divisible by $5.$

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=80$ rolls

- the probability of getting a number divisible by $5$ (i.e., a $5$ or a $10$) on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\frac{2}{12}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(80,\frac{1}{6}).$

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the  number of times we get a number divisible by $5$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{80\cdot \frac{1}{6}\cdot (1-\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =\sqrt{80\cdot \frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{5}{6}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{100}{9}} \\  & =\frac{10}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
